claim_text: Thames Valley Police arrested Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor on February 19, 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office and released him under investigation.
The Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as U.S. Attorney General on August 8, 2026 by a 50-49 vote.
A federal judge gave final approval on August 27, 2026 to Bank of America's $72.5 million class settlement with Epstein accusers.
President Trump removed Pam Bondi as U.S. Attorney General on April 2, 2026, and Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche became acting attorney general.

DOJ filed a notice of appeal of Judge Sullivan's September 16, 2026 order on September 17 and on September 22 asked the D.C. Circuit (No. 26-5299) to stay the foreign-language-records portions of the June 25 and September 16 orders and to expedite the appeal.

At the July 2, 2026 injunction deadline in Phang v. Blanche, DOJ declined to produce additional unredacted records, defended its redactions, and asked the court for 60 more days or to accept its reasons.

Reuters and CNN reported DOJ sent lawmakers a summary covering over 300 officials and politically exposed persons in Epstein-related records, while stating inclusion in that summary does not itself establish wrongdoing.
The DOJ Office of the Inspector General announced in April 2026 an audit of DOJ compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act.
Reuters reported DOJ sent lawmakers a Feb. 15, 2026 letter describing redaction rationale and stating four newly discussed individuals were not directly tied to wrongdoing in reviewed records.
Reps. Massie and Khanna said on September 18, 2026 that the discharge petition for the Epstein Files Transparency Act II had reached 218 signatures.
AP reported file excerpts described Epstein referencing Nobel committee leadership in outreach messages to high-profile contacts.

The Washington Post reported on September 9, 2026 that investigators in Poland, Norway, and Latvia said DOJ had not answered their mutual legal assistance requests; DOJ said it had not refused any jurisdiction.

On August 18, 2026 Magistrate Judge Ryon McCabe recommended that survivors' Federal Tort Claims Act negligence suit against the FBI, seeking about $320 million, proceed to 90 days of limited discovery.
The House voted on September 16, 2026 to hold Leon Black in contempt of Congress for defying House Oversight subpoenas in its Epstein investigation.
The Council of Europe waived Thorbjorn Jagland's immunity on February 11, 2026, and Okokrim charged him with aggravated corruption on February 12, 2026; he denies the charges.
Norway's Okokrim charged diplomat Mona Juul with aggravated corruption and her husband Terje Rod-Larsen with complicity in aggravated corruption on February 9, 2026.
Dean Kamen resigned from the FIRST board of directors on March 12, 2026; FIRST's board chair said its independent review found no evidence of misconduct.
AP reported some U.S. school districts paused or canceled Lifetouch sessions after viral posts made Epstein-related allegations.
AP reported Howard Lutnick acknowledged pre-government meetings with Epstein and that prior denials were inaccurate.
The Metropolitan Police arrested Peter Mandelson on February 23, 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office; he was later released under investigation.
Judge Paul Engelmayer denied Ghislaine Maxwell's pro se petition to vacate her conviction in an order made public on August 25, 2026.

New Mexico's Survivors' Truth Commission said its interim report found evidence supporting reports of sexual abuse of at least five women and girls at Zorro Ranch between 1996 and 2012, and that its final report is due December 31, 2026.
Norwegian and French investigators formed a joint investigation team in late April 2026 covering the case against Mona Juul and Terje Rod-Larsen.

Ohio State University's final report released June 23, 2026 found that Dr. Mark Landon was not aware of or involved in Epstein's crimes but likely violated university policy by not reporting or getting approval for outside consulting work.
On June 25, 2026, Judge Emmet Sullivan granted a preliminary injunction in Phang v. Blanche ordering DOJ to unredact disputed Epstein records or justify each redaction.

On August 11, 2026, Judge Loretta Preska ruled the Epstein Files Transparency Act overrides earlier sealing orders, grand-jury secrecy, and Ghislaine Maxwell's privacy claims, clearing additional records for release.
A federal judge unsealed on May 6, 2026 a purported note that Nicholas Tartaglione says he found in July 2019; the court did not assess its authenticity.

French model scout Daniel Siad, who was under French investigation over alleged recruitment for Epstein, was found dead at his home near Paris on July 20, 2026; the cause of death was under investigation.
UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced his resignation on June 22, 2026 amid fallout over his appointment of Peter Mandelson as ambassador.

On September 16, 2026 Judge Emmet Sullivan ordered DOJ to give the court, for private review, redacted and unredacted handwritten notes from four 2019 FBI interviews of a woman identified as Jane Doe 4 by 11 a.m. on September 24, and declined to stay the order pending appeal.

On September 16, 2026, Judge Sullivan set a September 24 deadline for DOJ to produce disputed Epstein records or explain why his orders were not clear, and said a contempt finding would be premature at that juncture.

Epstein survivors filed a proposed class action in the Northern District of California on March 26, 2026 against DOJ and Google, alleging the file releases exposed about 100 survivors' personal information and that Google kept republishing it.
AP reported Casey Wasserman planned to sell his talent agency after publication of emails involving Ghislaine Maxwell.

The Wall Street Journal reported on September 23, 2026 that federal prosecutors in Manhattan are investigating Epstein estate executors Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn; both deny wrongdoing and no charges have been filed.

Yale University barred computer science professor David Gelernter from teaching in February 2026 pending a conduct review of his emails with Epstein; in September 2026 Yale said the review was continuing and he would not teach in the fall.
